properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 17 at 6:07PM MDT until September 17 at 7:00PM MDT by NWS North Platte NE
properties.description:
SVRLBF

The National Weather Service in North Platte has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Southwestern Garden County in the Panhandle of Nebraska...
Northwestern Deuel County in the Panhandle of Nebraska...

* Until 700 PM MDT.

* At 607 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located over Lodgepole, or
7 miles northwest of Chappell, moving northeast at 20 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage
to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Chappell, Oshkosh, Mount Vernon, and Intersection of Highway 27 and
9 Mile Road.

This includes Interstate 80 in Nebraska between mile markers 78 and
85.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

To report severe weather, contact your nearest law enforcement
agency. They will send your report to the National Weather Service
office in North Platte.

Large hail, damaging wind, and continuous cloud to ground lightning
are occurring with this storm. Move indoors immediately. Lightning is
one of nature's leading killers. Remember, if you can hear thunder,
you are close enough to be struck by lightning.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 17 at 6:02PM MDT until September 17 at 6:30PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
At 602 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain over Blue 2 Burn Scar. Between 0.75 and 1.50 inches of rain have
fallen. Meanwhile, up to one third to one half an inch of rain has
fallen on the South Fork Burn Scar. Additional rainfall amounts of
0.25 to 1 inch are possible in the warned area as additional showers
and storms continue to develop. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will impact Upper Canyon, Brady
Canyon, and Perk Canyon as well as the Cedar Creek, Eagle Creek and
Rio Ruidoso drainages. Impacts will include but are not limited to
all nearby reservoirs, bridges, culverts and roadways.

HAZARD...Thunderstorms producing flash flooding in and around the
South Fork and Blue 2 Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
South Fork and Blue 2 Burn Scar.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Ruidoso, Alto, Bonito Lake and Hollywood.

Minor flooding and mud over roads have been reported in Upper Canyon
as a result of the South Fork Burn Scar.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks, streams and ditches in
the South Fork Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters, climb to safety.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 17 at 10:44AM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Levy, Marion and Citrus
Counties.

.The Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon (US 41) has been steadily
rising since July and on September 15, reached flood stage. The cause
of the high water along the Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon is
excessive hydrilla growth (from river bottom to the water surface)
along a 4.5 mile stretch of river between US 41 and Lake Rousseau.
The hydrilla is acting like a dam and holding water back, causing
water levels to rise.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:45 AM EDT Thursday the stage was 28.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:45 AM EDT Thursday was 28.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 28.2 feet.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.3
feet on 10/05/1965.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

through flooded areas.
